campaign: Integrated validation, phase 2: bounded capability gains and evidence-gated simplification
doctrine: Rank by fastest progress: model capability and validation first, then changes that make every later landing cheaper, then cleanup; owner-blocked and long-horizon rows last. Consolidate duplicated logic into fewer general components rather than adding instrumentation or frameworks; net AST nodes stay flat or fall, and the clone and harness ratchets hold the floor. Delete stale data and consolidate objects to reduce surface and improve robustness and efficiency: reviewed source lives in git, derived records in OvergoDB, process state in .overgo-runtime, and nothing a tool or evidence depends on lives in tmp. A consolidation row is done only when it deletes the implementations it replaces: test the shared owner's contract, keep only meaningful caller integration checks, retire tests of deleted wrappers, and report net production and test code removed, repeated executions eliminated, gate wall time and peak memory on comparable changes. Across the 197 first-parent commits to 2026-09-23, production Go grew about 9,000 net lines and tests about 11,600. OvergoDB keeps its core -- immutable content, a durable journal, aliases, rebuildable projections -- and the repository simplifies how it uses it, in order: integrity and blocking defects, one publication path, bounded queries, one record per transition, bounded memory, declared storage policy, then bounded segments. Store rows report bytes and records added per landing, records scanned per query, open and replay time, writer wait, peak memory and compaction write volume. No new model family, workflow, optimizer or orchestration framework without an owner request. A step's verify is its machine check; a check whose prerequisite cannot run records UNAVAILABLE, not a pass. depends_on names real producers. GUI and audio keep their lanes; master runs as master-lead. docs/plan.json is the only live plan.

items.title: Run every deferred lane from one build under one device claim

steps.title: Run every deferred lane from one build under one device claim
steps.rationale: Consolidation round 1. The device, test-device, model-journey and webui lanes each set up their own environment, compile their own binaries and take the GPU separately, so every landing builds about four near-duplicate trees (the Go build cache reached 759 GB and filled C: on 2026-09-25) and our own lanes contend for the device. Run every deferred lane in one process: one build of the candidate (with -trimpath, so worktrees share cache entries instead of each embedding its own path), one device claim, the suites in sequence, one verdict, each suite still reporting its own result. Lanes run from a frozen snapshot of their commit, not the live worktree: on 2026-09-25 starting a merge in the worktree killed the pending lane of c1b431d1 and it had to be re-run by hand. Device packages run one at a time (-p 1) in lanes and in test-lane receipts: a parallel receipt reserved the GPU against itself and timed out cuda/executor. The disk-full stop also failed a gate mid-run at checkout-index (GUI lane report, 2026-09-25): the gate refuses at admission when free space is below what its recent landings measurably consumed, naming the build cache as the usual cause, instead of failing mid-run -- a need measured from landing history, not a fixed reserve or cache cap. Absorbs device-claim-everywhere's lane half. Done when TestDeferredLanesShareOneBuild proves the lanes run from one build under one claim. Measured 2026-09-26: -trimpath cannot simply be added to the gate's builds -- under GOFLAGS=-trimpath the modern-Go census finds no candidates and runtime-input selection misreads packages (16 repoanalysis and 5 gate tests fail), because both match loaded positions by absolute file path. Path-independent cache sharing needs those analyses to key positions by module-relative path first; tests that locate the repository through runtime.Caller (plan, clioptions) would move to their working directory. Found 2026-09-26: the lane runner already executes every deferred lane in one process (executeDeferredLanes, one DAG) from a frozen candidate worktree (withCandidateWorktree over the fixed tree), and the device lanes already serialize through dependencies (webui, then journey, then test-device). Remaining: path-independent builds (blocked: -trimpath blinds the census), the disk-space admission from measured landing history, and receipts' serial packages (receipt-serial-packages).

items.title: Have every GPU user take the device claim lanes wait on

steps.title: Have every GPU user take the device claim lanes wait on
steps.rationale: Three sessions share one GPU. Preview servers started through launch.json hold the device while gate lanes time out behind them, and on 2026-09-23 a server of unknown origin was killed to free it. A served model should hold the same claim, so a lane waits for it and names it (01cbf544) instead of timing out. 2026-09-25: the device lane of 69368990 failed 'physical resource is already reserved' in devicemath while two other gate processes held the GPU, and passed unchanged on re-run; a claim every GPU user takes turns that into a wait with a named holder instead of a failed lane and a manual re-run.

items.title: Gate device and browser tests by detected capability, not environment variables

steps.title: Gate device and browser tests by detected capability, not environment variables
steps.rationale: OVERGO_CUDA_TEST, OVERGO_WEBUI_LANE, OVERGO_PROBE_TEST and per-model flags gate tests, and a skip-reason classifier recovers what they lose (fd3e2549). Detect the device and the browser once, skip with a classified reason when absent, and delete the variables. 2026-09-25: the reviewed media delta for the VAE port needed its device receipt run by hand with OVERGO_CUDA_TEST=1, OVERGO_WAN_MODEL pointing at the Wan checkpoint, -tags integration and -p 1; without them the Wan device tests silently skipped and the receipt proved nothing about the changed paths. Resolve a test's model through the store by identity (models-resolve-by-identity) and its device by detection, so a receipt over a package runs its real-model tests without an operator knowing the switches.

items.title: Run every gate check as a rule in one registry over one parse, fixing mechanical findings

steps.title: Run every gate check as a rule in one registry over one parse, fixing mechanical findings
steps.rationale: Consolidation round 1, refactor 1 (owner 2026-09-25: two or more birds with one stone; minimize to the maximum practical extent; no ledgers where construction can prevent the object). Measured: 1560 landing attempts, 844 succeeded; of 1055 failed steps about 73% (excluding the retired remote-provider check) were static or bookkeeping -- magics 276, profile 107, style 59, protection 43, claims 41, modern-go 23, scope 15, architecture 15, docs 13, fmt 12, sbom 10. internal/gate grew from 0 to 16k production and 26k test lines in 40 days, about 170 test files one per incident. Make every static check a rule in one registry (name, applies-to change set, check, and a fix for mechanical findings) run over one parse of the candidate tree, in parallel by package, each rule still reporting its own finding and evidence. Mechanical findings are fixed by the same pass in the developer loop (preflight), so the gate only confirms and the preflight result is the gate's static result. Fold closurescan, closureledger and cmd/closure-scan in as a rule; merge automationcheck, testevidence and testscope into the gate's selection. Replace the per-incident test files with one corpus of example change sets (extend false_negative_corpus_test.go). Net-negative is enforced by the automation- prefix. Done when TestGateRulesRunFromOneRegistry proves every static check runs from the registry over one parse and a mechanical finding is fixed, not refused. Progress 2026-09-26: L1 landed (438dc817, the gateRules table), the owns column and one path catalog landed (66be7333), and the gate already rebinds drifted closure bindings in magics, so the manual rebind is not needed. Measured: one discovery and parse of the whole tree costs about 0.55 s serial (3854 files, 0.13 s read, 0.42 s parse), so sharing one parse across the static checks saves about a second of CPU in parallel steps -- low yield; re-ranked below automation-order-by-cost-and-yield. The remaining value is mechanical fixes in the developer loop and folding the per-incident tests into one corpus.

items.title: Prevent ledgered objects by construction and derive the remaining ledgers at gate time

steps.title: Prevent ledgered objects by construction and derive the remaining ledgers at gate time
steps.rationale: Consolidation round 1, refactor 2. About 48k Go lines maintain 40 committed JSON ledgers; 78% of commits touch a generated file and plan.json changed in 543 of the last 552 commits. Owner rule: no ledger where construction can prevent the object -- literals come only from one typed policy/config source, shared operations live in one package, a new export arrives with its consumer. Where construction cannot prevent it, derive the document from the tree at gate time (one internal/ledger mechanism, one cmd/census -kind command replacing modern-census, rsi-census, clone-census, mechanism-census, api-manifest, code-manifest, profile-catalog, coverage-lanes, block-check, store-check, store-precheck) and commit only reviewed floors and exceptions. Take row status out of plan.json (the commit trailer and the store already hold it). Stop committing .ptx and media_report.json. Done when TestLedgersDeriveFromTheTree proves the derived documents equal the committed ones they replace and no landing writes them.

items.title: Declare every store record kind in one table

steps.title: Declare every store record kind in one table
steps.rationale: Consolidation round 1, refactor 3. The store has 453 distinct schema strings, 330 media-type constants, 231 contract literals, 31 codecs and 23 hand-written mirror structs (0 -> 453 schemas from Aug 5 to Sep 25), mostly in runrecord and evaluation: one schema per claim. Declare every record kind once in a single kind/version table with a generic artifact.Record[T]; derive schema string and media type from it; decode and encode through struct tags and strictjson instead of hand-written mirrors and closures; merge runrecord's attempt_*, automation_*, peer_*, lane_* and resource_fitness* families into a few general records. Stored documents stay readable (versioned decode). Done when TestRecordKindsDeclaredInOneTable proves every stored kind resolves from the table and no schema literal lives outside it.

steps.title: Resolve lane evidence from one store without imports

steps.title: Fold per-modality commands into route tables
steps.rationale: Consolidation round 1, refactor 5. 102 commands (25 at the start): 10 train probes, 9 lanes, 6 parity or oracle commands, 14 model-file tools, 5 store tools. Fold them into route tables: the probes become routes of cmd/train -route (docs/training_routes.json, one objective mode for every objective kind: forecast, tabular and text fold into cmd/train -objective), the lanes become cmd/gate -lane, parity tools become cmd/validate -parity, the gguf and inspect tools become cmd/gguf subcommands, the overgodb tools cmd/overgodb subcommands. items.title: Re-acquire pinned identities automatically when the surface moves

steps.title: Re-acquire pinned identities automatically when the surface moves
steps.rationale: Consolidation round 1, refactor 6. The inference-surface digest and the media runtime hash turn every file move into a delta and a re-acquisition: 35 commits were manual re-acquire or refresh work. Key guards and media deltas by the surface digest held in the store and re-acquire them automatically when the surface moves (cmd/loop surface move), in the same landing. Two further birds from 2026-09-25: (1) narrow the surface to what inference executes -- the hidden-console fix to internal/processcontrol and the audio lane's internal/optimizer restore each expired every text guard although neither runs in text inference; (2) build a reviewed media delta from its receipt in one command -- file hashes, the device receipt with its model resolved, required tests chosen from the passing tests that exercise the changed files, and the registry identity -- instead of the hand-assembled JSON and constant edit the VAE port needed. Absorbs surface-move-preflight; guards-reacquire-lane and surface-without-capability-tables follow it. Done when TestSurfaceMoveReacquiresPinnedIdentities proves a surface move lands with its identities re-acquired and no manual row.

items.title: Re-acquire expired text guards in a deferred lane

steps.title: Re-acquire expired text guards in a deferred lane
steps.rationale: Automation friction: a landing that moves the inference surface expires every text guard (10 models), and re-acquisition is manual: longform -guard-coverage -all -publish at about 8 minutes per model, run from a detached scratch worktree at HEAD because -publish needs a clean tree (cc73695a). The pending GUI arch-event-hub merge had to be batched with master's next surface move for this reason alone. When a landed commit moves the surface, queue guard re-acquisition as a deferred lane at that commit. Its results publish into the store, and the next gate waits for its verdict like the device lanes. Reuse the device claim and the existing deferred-lane scheduler; add no scheduler. Done when TestSurfaceMoveQueuesGuardReacquisition shows a surface-moving landing queues the lane and a non-moving one does not.

items.title: Split the profile's commands into runtime and automation by declaration

steps.title: Split the profile's commands into runtime and automation by declaration
steps.rationale: Deferred from automation-path-surface-catalog (2026-09-26): codeprofile counts every cmd/ Go file in the Automation partition, so product commands (server, swap, train, generate, the gguf and hf converters, embedding, rerank, tokenize, ...) inflate the automation figure the delta advisory reports and skew any ROI read of it. The split is a per-command owner decision: declare it once in the path catalog (codeprofile.Classify's Automation class) as the harness command set -- gate, loop, plan, the censuses, the lanes, closure-scan, finding, guard and the like -- rather than inferring it from names. items.title: Re-measure growth and gate failures, then file the next consolidation round

steps.title: Re-measure growth and gate failures, then file the next consolidation round
steps.rationale: Owner 2026-09-25: after refactor 6, step back and run the whole consolidation loop again, a few rounds, until a round finds little left to merge. Re-measure growth by pattern, gate failure causes by rule, duplicates and churn (from the rule registry, the derived ledgers and store history rather than a manual analysis), rank the patterns, file round 3's rows, and record the round's before/after counts (landing wall, rules, commands, packages, schemas, lines). Also measure the work per change: landings per delivered row (2026-09-25: 16 landings for 3 merges, one port and one fix), refusals by cause and manual re-runs, so the round ranks what costs the operator the most. Done when cmd/census -kind consolidation -round 2 prints the recorded round and its filed rows.

items.title: Carry the VAE lane's latent campaign surface until the lane closes it

steps.title: Carry the VAE lane's latent campaign surface until the lane closes it
steps.rationale: The overgo_vae lane (branch codex/overgo_vae, campaign overgo_rsi_with_vae, design docs/overgo_rsi_with_vae.md) runs the native-Go latent RSI and PEARL campaign with its own plan in its own worktree. Owner decision 2026-09-25: master takes the lane in parts that have a production consumer, not whole. Master ported the runtime part at e1ee1326fe2b (row vae-codec-stream-port: media.CodecChunkStream owning causal codec state, the Wan VAE host and CUDA encode and CUDA decode through it; the host streaming DecodeLatentVideo stays a test on master until it has a production caller); the ported files are byte-identical to the lane's, so merging master back is clean. DIRECTION FOR THE LANE when it merges master (master is in a consolidation-only phase: two birds with one stone, minimize to the maximum practical extent, no ledger where construction can prevent the object): (1) consumer first -- land each latent contract (representation latent state and codec, geometry, tensorstats resampling and robust scalars, media latent volume) together with its first production consumer; the first merge unit is first-latent-capability/existing-vae-inference-proof, and no export arrives without a caller; (2) no new record families -- express experimental evidence through the shared record table that automation-one-record-table builds instead of runrecord experimental_* families, and keep campaign-history adoption out of master's internal/plan; (3) reconcile pinned media runtime moves with a reviewed delta in docs/media_reviewed_deltas.json backed by a device receipt, never by narrowing TestReviewedDeltaRegistryExplainsTheTree; (4) never raise docs/clone_baseline.json -- the merged tree measured 7964 against master's 7991 while the lane raised it to 9970; (5) after merging master, drop the lane's testCodecChunkState copy in internal/media/codec_latent_test.go: master's TestCodecChunkStreamOwnsCausalState owns it; (6) keep evidence identities in compatibility.json refreshed from master's store, not the lane's. Master keeps its plan; any staged surface a later merge brings retires with this row. Done when the lane's campaign closeout has merged and TestVAECampaignClosedOut proves no staged entry names this row.

items.title: Store gate telemetry and merge authority by reference

steps.title: Store gate telemetry and merge authority by reference
steps.rationale: Follow-up of store-benchmark-record-redundancy, measured at 7f700241. A code landing still stores the suite cost (103 KB: 1,094 test rows each repeating the package; package_execution_cost.go:85) and the selection cause (52 KB, 96% of its reader graph repeated from the previous landing; batch_cost.go:205). items.title: Report private code only tests reach as review candidates

steps.title: Report private code only tests reach as review candidates
steps.rationale: SQA-013's detector half, re-scoped by owner direction 2026-09-24: a finding of no callers is a question, not a deletion order. The unconsumed-surface rule sees exported declarations with no production consumer, but not private code reachable only through them; that is how the seq2seq trainer went unnoticed as unwired. Compute unconsumed private code transitively over ProductionConsumerGraph, with reflection and cgo boundaries counted as consumers, and report each island as a review candidate classified by what it is: a training or inference capability to wire, test support to move, or code a named wired replacement supersedes. It refuses nothing on its own. Done when TestPrivateCodeReachedOnlyByTestsIsFound reports a private helper reached only from a test-only exported function in a fixture, and not one also reached from a live root.

items.title: Run or delete tests no lane enables

steps.title: Run or delete tests no lane enables
steps.rationale: From consolidation-inventory (2026-09-24): 283 OVERGO_* environment reads sit in tests; 151 names appear only in tests and 145 of those are documented nowhere. 130 test functions (about 12,000 lines) skip unless a variable is set, and the lanes set only OVERGO_CUDA_TEST, OVERGO_WEBUI_LANE, OVERGO_WEBUI_LANE_SCREENS and OVERGO_BROWSER, so about 82 of them (about 5,800 lines, heaviest in internal/inference, adaptiveparity and projector) never run in any gate. Owner direction 2026-09-24: training and inference validation is the point of overgo, so give each a lane that runs it, with its model or data declared. Delete only a test a named running test supersedes. The same holds for modeltest-tagged suites no lane runs, such as seq2seq's GSM8K training suite. The probe is tmp/envgate_probe.go. Done when TestEveryTestGateIsSetByALane holds.

items.title: Declare storage class and retention on the document contract

steps.title: Declare storage class and retention on the document contract
steps.rationale: Storage classes are chosen by schema-name substrings (heartbeat, wakeup, poll, partial-output, liveness in storage_classes.go:34), a parallel registry that drifts from the contracts. Declare storage class, retention and publication owner beside each document contract, and delete the substring list. Retention separates required acceptance and recovery evidence from replaceable summaries and diagnostic detail, derives reports from retained results, and keeps explicit roots for outstanding work. Backup pruning stays operator policy.

items.title: Track golden generators and keep golden provenance in the store

steps.title: Track golden generators and keep golden provenance in the store
steps.rationale: Golden outputs are tracked (testdata, fixtures), but their generators and inputs (timesfm3_golden.py, dinov2_golden.py, generate_kimi_k3_rank_reference.py, their input and spec JSON) exist only in tmp, and internal/parity/testdata/make_olmoe_tiny.py is the one generator still in the tree. Put generators in one tracked directory, the only place Python is allowed. Record each golden in the store with its reference commit, checkpoint identity, generator and inputs, and have the test check its testdata file against that record. Large goldens live only in the store. The Colibri2 merge (2026-09-25) moved the Kimi K3 rank generator from internal/hfbpe/testdata to tmp, consistent with the others; its fixture kimi_k3_rank_reference.json keeps its source provenance (repository, commit, sha256).

items.title: Store medium payloads in immutable, size-bounded pack segments

steps.title: Store medium payloads in immutable, size-bounded pack segments
steps.rationale: After the publication, query and memory rows land, and only from measured record sizes, read patterns and compaction cost. Small transition records stay inline in journal entries, medium immutable payloads go to bounded pack segments, large tensors, media and logs to individually addressed blobs, indexes and checkpoints to replaceable derived generations, and live progress to bounded runtime state. Adding a small record must not rewrite an ever-growing pack, and one enormous file would trade file count for rewrite and recovery cost. Done when compaction write volume and open and replay time fall on the measured store without losing backup or recovery.

items.title: Narrow what a confined landing re-runs by a checked reach contract

steps.title: Narrow what a confined landing re-runs by a checked reach contract
steps.rationale: A one-command landing runs about 29 packages (170 s work, 80 s wall), 28 of them for an unnamed reach inherited through overgodb, artifact, gitauthority, gosource and repoanalysis. Syntactic rules were measured unsound. Either a package declares its reach confined to caller-supplied roots and its tests fail on a read outside them, or a receipt's inputs become the files its tests opened. Keep the shadow measure and reader ranking as before and after.

items.title: Cut the gate suite's longest tests

steps.title: Cut the gate suite's longest tests
steps.rationale: Measured 2026-09-23 at 83d0bb9b: suite 149-155 s. The critical path is the live fixture's single lock: ready at about 33 s, then 14 seeded plans run one at a time for about 103 s, and TestTestingReductionContract's five plans end the suite alone. Each plan recomputes whole-snapshot analyses for a one-file seed (codeprofile.Build 14 s, the consumer graph through go list 15 s, manifest identity 10 s and diff 6 s, CPU over five plans), so the content-keyed manifest cache never hits. Warming the base manifest in the fixture measured no gain. A pool of checkouts costs about 40 s of cold setup per extra slot and reverses the one-checkout budget. The structural lever is incremental analysis keyed per file or package (profile facts and consumer-graph edges reused for unchanged files), which also shortens every production gate's base-versus-candidate manifests.

items.title: Defer decoding large store facets until first use, if opens are still slow

steps.title: Defer decoding large store facets until first use, if opens are still slow
steps.rationale: Re-measured 2026-09-24 after store-open-decode-cost (180a7a3c): an open takes about 1.05-1.5 s and allocates 1.8 GB; checkpoint decode is 56% of it (lineage 0.6 s) and replaying the 8,100 commits since the last checkpoint is 32%. Before that, 2026-09-22: a read-only open is 1.7 s, bounded by the largest decode (lineage 88.3 MB of 189 MB), with verification about 0.1 s. Laziness inside the facet fails (value receivers) and re-replaying the journal fails (shared file cursor). Defer at the store, which owns the lock: keep the verified payload and pending commits, apply on first load behind a double-checked write lock, and test that a deferred facet answers exactly as an eager one.

items.title: Decide the 12B FP8 checkpoints on measured quantization loss

steps.title: Decide the 12B FP8 checkpoints on measured quantization loss
steps.rationale: OWNER DECISION: download the unquantized google/gemma-4-12B-it checkpoint? The 12B twins score 0.5-1.2 nats per token worse than E4B on the guard corpus (3.17 vs 1.48 on plain English), raw or chat-framed. overgo's 12B graph matches the transformers reference point by point (layers within 2.6e-4, logits within about 0.2 of adaptive_new's golden), so the suspect is the third-party FP8 quant both twins come from. Re-scoped per SQA-012: closure no longer requires a 12B to outscore E4B, a different model. The row answers three separate questions, with tokenization, template, scoring windows and tolerances frozen before the run: (1) runtime agreement on a matched checkpoint, already held against the golden; (2) the FP8 twins' quality loss against the bf16 original on the same windows, which needs the owner's download; (3) whether that loss is acceptable, the owner's product target. E4B stays a comparator. Done when TestGemmaTwelveCheckpointVerdict records a verdict for the FP8 twins: kept with the measured loss, or rejected as a checkpoint, with the matched-checkpoint agreement as evidence.

items.title: Stop compatibility reports churning every landing (owner decision first)

steps.title: Stop compatibility reports churning every landing (owner decision first)
steps.rationale: OWNER DECISION: does a claim's file:sha256 source binding mean re-verify when the code moves (then a refresh re-runs the claim's oracle), or nothing (then it leaves both documents)? Then docs/model_compatibility.json and docs/media_report.json leave the tree, and performance_sweep_baseline.json keeps its thresholds with measurements in the store.

items.title: Key cmd/compatibility's receipt to the files it actually reads

steps.title: Key cmd/compatibility's receipt to the files it actually reads
steps.rationale: The input graph treats the package as an opaque reader, binding it to every root (269 packages) including docs/plan.json, so the complete receipt for ten media and specialized models expires on every landing and costs a four-minute rerun. Found 2026-09-23, three sources of the binding: (1) reads join a root parameter that production only ever passes as ".", which in-package parameter propagation in the classifier would name; (2) the operator verbs (claim, record-verification, webui-report) read flag paths and can move to their own command; (3) -check reads the source files docs/compatibility.json binds to each claim, so part of the broad binding is correct until compatibility-reports-leave-the-tree decides what that binding means. Waits on that decision; (1) and (2) alone leave the package opaque.
